schema: Time Twist complete translation workbook v1
source_of_truth: japanese_exact is decoded from immutable Japanese banks; annotations are editorial aids
exact_japanese_policy: Exact Japanese is copied from the decoded ROM corpus. Reconstructed Japanese is editorial and conservative.

control_legend.CTRL:0: Observed mainly as a dialogue-row or line advance. Exact runtime behavior depends on the surrounding script routine.
control_legend.CTRL:1: Observed as a stronger paragraph/page transition or staged reveal. Preserved without translating it.
control_legend.CTRL:2: Observed at page/box transitions and speaker-sequence breaks. Preserved without asserting a single universal meaning.
control_legend.CTRL:3: Observed in multi-page continuation/timing sequences and sometimes near animation or input boundaries.
control_legend.CTRL:4: Observed in continuation/timing sequences; often alternates with CTRL:3 while the text buffer advances.
control_legend.CTRL:6: Observed as a major wait/page/scene beat. Exact behavior requires runtime tracing for each call site.

TT1A.title: 1995 prologue, fortune service, and personality test
TT1A.summary: On September 25, 1995, a newscast introduces physicist Dr. Simon's time-travel research. A televised fortune service collects the player's blood type, birth month, and yes/no personality answers, then predicts a meeting at a suburban museum. The narration establishes a polluted, anxious near-future Japan.
TT1A.choices: The personality-test prompts are Japanese declarative propositions answered yes/no. Natural English questions are used where that makes the interface clearer without changing the proposition.

TT1B.title: Devil Museum, possession, Dr. Simon, and the first time warp
TT1B.summary: The protagonist reaches the Devil Museum, meets a mysterious girl, and triggers exhibits tied to a sealed Devil. Comic flirting, a Nagoya/Owari-coded businessman, a church, and Dr. Simon's Time Belt lead into the first historical jump.
TT1B.choices: The protagonist normally labels himself おれ, but switches to gentler ぼく when protecting or reassuring the girl. The Devil's pompous voice and the businessman's clustered regional caricature are kept distinct.

TT2.title: 1428 France: Pierre, Jeanne d'Arc, and the witch hunt
TT2.summary: The protagonist arrives in 1428 France by possessing Pierre. He navigates a town, solves comic quizzes, meets Jeanne, and learns that the Bishop is exploiting a witch hunt under the Devil's influence.
TT2.choices: Rough commoner speech, official/church formality, and stock elderly role-language are differentiated. Jeanne is 'Jeanne' in dialogue and 'Jeanne d'Arc' in historical narration.

T22.title: France continuation: the prison, the pact, and the rescue
T22.summary: The Baron and jailer confront evidence of the Bishop's demonic pact. The protagonist works through the prison and execution grounds to save Jeanne and expose the Bishop.
T22.choices: The pact uses elevated, deliberately archaic diction; ordinary prison dialogue does not. Ecclesiastical titles remain titles rather than personal names.

TT3A.title: 1944 Germany: POW camp, resistance network, and escape
TT3A.summary: The protagonist becomes U.S. airman Cougar in a southern German POW camp. He escapes through a tunnel, encounters Simon and the Rebecca resistance network, and navigates Gestapo surveillance and coded clues.
TT3A.choices: Military ranks and Nazi terminology are translated plainly. The fragmented blue-note clue is layout-dependent and remains flagged for visual verification.

TT3B.title: 1944 Germany continuation: Schmidt, Hitler, and the border
TT3B.summary: Schmidt appears to capture Cougar and Simon but reveals himself as a resistance ally. Their flight toward Switzerland becomes a direct confrontation with Hitler under supernatural influence.
TT3B.choices: Simon remains formal and idealistic; Schmidt is terse and controlled. The script's caricature of Hitler is translated without embellishing or softening it.

TT4.title: Ancient Athens and the Greek underworld
TT4.summary: The protagonist appears as the physician Nicras in ancient Athens, revives a priest, receives Athena's plea, treats townspeople, and descends through mythological territory involving Hermes, Hades, Artemis, Poseidon, and Cerberus.
TT4.choices: Greek names use established English forms. よみのくに is rendered contextually as the underworld rather than importing a Japanese Shinto cosmology into the Greek setting.

TT5.title: September 1864 Atlanta: slavery, emancipation, and plantation life
TT5.summary: The protagonist becomes George, a Black farmhand living with his mother Belle near Atlanta during the American Civil War. The chapter depicts racist violence, emancipation, plantation labor, Lincoln, and puzzles involving farm work and livestock.
TT5.choices: The source's racist and dated material is translated directly, not sanitized. Enslaved characters' stylized Japanese speech is rendered as rural/working-class English without exaggerated minstrel dialect.

T25.title: Civil War continuation: Meyer, Lincoln, and the river escape
T25.summary: The plantation storyline continues through Meyer's mansion, a meeting with Lincoln, armed guards, and an escape sequence involving George, Belle, a boat, and coyotes.
T25.choices: Meyer's self-serving politeness and Lincoln's measured formality are kept separate. Political claims are translated as character dialogue, not endorsed narration.

TT6A.title: Circa 4 BC Nazareth: Joseph, Mary, and Kashim the donkey
TT6A.summary: The protagonist becomes Joseph's donkey Kashim in Nazareth. Joseph struggles with Mary's pregnancy, the village debates prophecy and Roman rule, and a census order begins the journey to Bethlehem.
TT6A.choices: Biblical names use familiar English forms. Elderly じゃ/のう speech is treated as role-language, while the protagonist's donkey sounds and inner monologue retain the chapter's comedy.

TT6B.title: Journey to Bethlehem: desert trials, riddles, and animal comedy
TT6B.summary: Joseph, Mary, and Kashim cross barren country, seek food and water, solve direction and identity riddles, and meet talking animals before reaching Bethlehem.
TT6B.choices: Animal voices remain comic without becoming children's-book baby talk. Marked forms such as だっぺ are treated as characterization, not proof that the setting itself has a Japanese regional dialect.

TT6C.title: Nativity climax and final confrontation
TT6C.summary: At the Nativity, the Devil attempts revenge. The Magi, Joseph, Mary, Kashim, and the restored protagonist fight possession and work to save the infant Jesus before the story returns to 1995.
TT6C.choices: Caspar, Melchior, and Balthazar use dignified diction. The Devil's archaizing self-importance contrasts with the protagonist's blunt modern voice.

TT6D.title: Epilogue in 1995
TT6D.summary: The protagonist and the girl awaken in the present. She does not remember their shared history, but her fortune and the recurring incantation close the romantic and supernatural loops.
TT6D.choices: The girl's feminine sentence endings are conveyed through warmth and confidence, not a caricatured accent. The final growl remains deliberately ominous.

NOV2.title: System menu and disk-change prompts
NOV2.summary: Start, wait, disk-side, insertion, and wrong-disk messages.
NOV2.choices: Uppercase is retained for system text; exact packed slots govern abbreviations.

NOV4.title: Title-screen start prompt
NOV4.summary: The fixed start-menu label loaded with the title program.

TITLE.title: Title graphics
TITLE.summary: English wordmark and subtitle represented as graphics rather than scenario records.
TITLE.choices: The requested subtitle is retained exactly.

SON-KOUH.title: Kouhen direct-boot guard
SON-KOUH.summary: Graphics text instructing the player to begin by loading Zenpen.
SON-KOUH.choices: Natural English is expanded; the graphic itself remains a separate technical asset.

speaker_reference.name: Protagonist
speaker_reference.labels: おれ; occasionally ぼく inside speech
speaker_reference.first_person: おれ (rough/plain masculine); ぼく when softening his tone
speaker_reference.endings: plain modern speech; ぞ/な/だ; frequent stutters and exclamations
speaker_reference.habits: internal commentary, comic panic, flirtation, abrupt disbelief
speaker_reference.relationships: player viewpoint; protects the girl; pursues the Devil and Simon
speaker_reference.english_voice: quick, contemporary, wry, and emotionally transparent; not macho parody

speaker_reference.name: Girl
speaker_reference.endings: feminine-coded わ/の and polite forms where appropriate
speaker_reference.relationships: modern woman tied to the museum incident and epilogue
speaker_reference.english_voice: warm and poised, capable of teasing; avoid exaggerated femininity

speaker_reference.name: Devil
speaker_reference.endings: じゃ/のう/ぞ and grand declaratives
speaker_reference.dialect: stock archaizing old-man/authority role-language, not a firm region
speaker_reference.relationships: possessor and antagonist across all historical chapters
speaker_reference.english_voice: grandiose, sardonic, old-fashioned when useful; never generic rural dialect

speaker_reference.name: Dr. Simon
speaker_reference.labels: しもん; しもんはかせ
speaker_reference.habits: scientific explanation, ethical reflection, hesitation under pressure
speaker_reference.relationships: physicist behind the Time Belt; recurring ally and target

speaker_reference.name: Nagoya/Owari-coded businessman
speaker_reference.endings: がや/で; どえりゃー; うるしゃー; くりゃーて
speaker_reference.habits: money obsession and oversized resort plans
speaker_reference.relationships: comic modern encounter near the museum
speaker_reference.english_voice: brash regional-businessman flavor without mapping him to one real U.S. region

speaker_reference.name: Pierre and medieval commoners
speaker_reference.labels: ぴえーる; ちの; ごるどー; るごー
speaker_reference.dialect: stylized commoner speech, not geographically Japanese in the fiction
speaker_reference.english_voice: earthy medieval-adventure dialogue; readable, not faux-Shakespearean

speaker_reference.name: Bishop
speaker_reference.endings: archaizing じゃ/おれ commands under demonic influence
speaker_reference.dialect: role-language rather than a regional diagnosis
speaker_reference.relationships: antagonist in the Jeanne d'Arc chapter
speaker_reference.english_voice: self-important ecclesiastical authority with theatrical menace

speaker_reference.name: Schmidt
speaker_reference.habits: controlled speech and concealed resistance allegiance
speaker_reference.relationships: apparent Nazi officer; ally to Cougar and Simon
speaker_reference.english_voice: clipped and disciplined, softening only after his reveal

speaker_reference.name: Belle and George
speaker_reference.politeness: deferential under coercion; intimate in private
speaker_reference.dialect: source uses stylized nonstandard Japanese to mark class/setting
speaker_reference.habits: Belle is protective and devout; George is direct and frightened
speaker_reference.relationships: mother and son on Meyer's farm
speaker_reference.english_voice: plain rural speech with dignity; avoid minstrel caricature

speaker_reference.name: Joseph
speaker_reference.politeness: familiar with Kashim; respectful to officials/elders

speaker_reference.name: Village Elder
speaker_reference.english_voice: measured elder voice; lightly old-fashioned, never hillbilly
